    * Metadata from youtube.com is used for ytmusic
  * [Twitch live streams have out of sync audio and lowered pitch #4280](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4280)
    * Use `--live-from-start` or `--fixup never`
  * [Cannot download video from udemy #1164](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1164)
  * [\--trim-filenames fails to clip file name properly when there is a dot in a video title #2314](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2314)
    * Use `-o %(title).200B.%(ext)s`
  * [[teachable] ERROR: Unable to find Video URL https://edu.ecomsuccess.pk/courses/enrolled/903296 #3564](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3564)
  * [CeskaTelevize broken #6539](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6539)
  * [iQIYI extractor can't find any video #2740](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2740)
  * [[Viu] URLs are using generic extractor instead of Viu extractor #6482](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6482)
  * [[abciview + others] ERROR: Data must be padded to 16 byte boundary in CBC mode #3810](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3810)
  * [[Ixigua] ERROR: Failed to get SSR_HYDRATED_DATA #5374](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5374)
  * [Douyin always errors saying fresh cookies are needed, even when passing them #9667](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9667)
  * **[[TikTok:live] Livestreams are mistaken as "not currently live" after JSON metadata request #11921](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11921)**
  * **[[tiktok:live] Unable to download JSON metadata: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request #16850](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16850)**
  * [[tiktok] API returns empty response #13134](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13134)
  * [[TikTok] One format, varying results (region-related) #15690](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15690)
  * **[[TikTok] Unable to extract universal data for rehydration #17393](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17393)**
  * [Only audio downloads for TikTok videos that have a shopping cart #13928](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13928)
  * **[[BiliBili] Unable to download webpage: HTTP Error 412: Precondition Failed #14830](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14830)**
  * [[LinkedIn] Unable to extract video from LinkedIn group post #16531](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16531)



# External issues

  * **[[Youtube] HTTP Error 403 when using bgutil-ytdlp-pot-provider plugin #17368](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17368)**
  * [ffmpeg can't seek in Youtube's iOS m3u8 streams / `--download-sections` only downloads audio #9552](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9552)
    * Use `-S proto:https` or `--extractor-args "youtube:player_client=default,-ios"`
  * [`--cookies-from-browser` "Permission denied" errors when Chrome/chromium-based browser is open in Windows #7271](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7271)
    * Try after closing chrome completely OR
    * Launch chrome from command line w/ `chrome.exe --disable-features=LockProfileCookieDatabase`
    * Alternatively, you can [install](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#installing-plugins) the [ChomeCookieUnlock yt-dlp plugin](https://github.com/seproDev/yt-dlp-ChromeCookieUnlock)
  * [`--cookies-from-browser`: WARNING: failed to decrypt with DPAPI / ERROR: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'decode' #10927](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10927)
  * [[youtube] Is downloading a livestream in 1440p or 2160p no longer available? #11262](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11262)
  * [[Youtube] 8k VR180 SBS videos no longer available #9903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/9903)
    * Use `--extractor-arg "youtube:player_client=android_vr,default"`
  * [[Youtube] throttling and inconsistent speed in Russia #10443](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443)
    * [Workarounds](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10443#issuecomment-2248940967)
  * [[Discord bot] Music stops in the middle #8854](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8854)
  * [[youtube] Endless "Incomplete data received" when downloading playlist #10394](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10394)
    * Don't use `--extractor-retries infinite`
  * [FFMPEG "Invalid data found when processing input" on live/post-live/dash videos (duplicate ftyp) #8641](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8641)
    * Regression in ffmpeg 6.1. Upgrade to ffmpeg 6.1.1 or to [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases) revision `N-112916` or later
  * [[youtube] "Invalid data found when processing input" / ffmpeg errors on HDR VP9 in mp4 #7541](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7541)
    * ffmpeg bug. Upgrade to ffmpeg 7.0.1 or to the latest [master build](https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds/releases)
  * [`--mark-watched` fails with urlopen error #8149](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8149)
    * Disable pi-hole or whitelist `s.youtube.com`
  * [Chapter Embedding Results in Unnamed Chapters When Using Recent FFmpeg Builds #6859](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6859)
    * ffmpeg regression. Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/FFmpeg-Builds> or upgrade to 6.1.1 or newer
  * [yt-dlp is detected as a virus #25](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/25)
    * It's a false positive. Complain to your vendor. There is nothing we can do
  * [Incomplete Data Recieved #1787](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1787)
    * Broken from Youtube's side. If downloading comments, use `-i` to ignore the error
  * [Wrong year in metadata in M4A, MP4, FLAC format #3087](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3087)
    * Workaround: `--parse-metadata "%(release_year,upload_date).4s:(?P<meta_date>.+)"`
  * [pyinstaller temp files are not cleaned up when using yt-dlp.exe with mpv #10294](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10294)
  * [Long Start-Up Time for `yt-dlp_macos` #10425](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10425)
  * [`--download-sections` / ffmpeg fails to seek in a 26+ hour long Twitch m3u8 #5372](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5372)
  * [Using proxy and `--download-sections`/ ffmpeg fails with HTTP Error 400/401/403 #12915](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12915)



# FAQ

See <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ>

  * **[How to avoid Youtube's new "Super Resolution" AI-upscaled formats #15325](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15325)**
  * **[Getting deno to work in Termux. #15095 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15095#issuecomment-3544324838)**
    * Run a full Termux upgrade with `pkg update && pkg upgrade` before `pkg install deno`
  * **[[YouTube] Enhanced bitrate no longer available to download? #14133 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14133#issuecomment-3217679575)**
  * [**Filename too long**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136#issuecomment-932077195)
    * Use `-o "%(title).150B [%(id)s].%(ext)s"`
  * **[[YouTube]`--write-comments`: "Incomplete data received. Giving up after 3 retries" warnings #15435](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15435)**
  * **[twitter: No video could be found in this tweet #14742](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14742)**
  * [[Question] odd ba* format selection? #979 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/979#issuecomment-919629354)
    * Generally do not use `ba*`
  * [Fix playlist_index's inconsistent behavior #302](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/302)
    * Check `playlist_autonumber` and `--compat-option playlist-index`
  * [yt-dlp python module not compiling with pyinstaller #3845](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3845)
    * Use `bundle/pyinstaller.py`
  * [Subtitle file is not deleted after being embedded #630 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/630#issuecomment-893659460)
    * Use `--compat-option no-keep-subs`
  * [`--download-sections`/`--sponsorblock-remove` does not cut at exact point #4216](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4216) / [YouTube Clip Downloads have unintented extra beginning part with no video #5080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5080)
    * Use `--force-keyframes-at-cuts`
  * [Duplicating pull request from youtube-dl to yt-dlp #4202](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4202)
  * [How to check in browser if the video is DRM protected](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4062#issuecomment-1153474056)
  * [\--cookies-from-browser for a chrome/firefox like browser or non-default install location #2903](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2903)
  * [What are yt-dlp's error codes? #4262 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4262#issuecomment-1173133105)
  * [Extractor option `language` for `crunchyrollbeta` #4640](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4640)
  * [Ability to strip Emoji from downloaded file  #4836](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/4836) / [File names use "full-width" special characters: '？' vs '?' #5014](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5014)
  * [[Youtube] Extract exact timestamps #1803](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1803)
  * [[Feature Request] Crop to square thumbnail when embedding in MP3s #429 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/429#issuecomment-2282554440)
  * Download only videos with subtitles 
    * `--parse-metadata "%(subtitles.\:.0.ext|)s:^(?!\[\])(?P<has_subs>.)" -v --match-filter has_subs`
  * [How do I rename previously-downloaded files with nothing but the youtube video ID? #5692](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5692)
  * Remove specific fields from info-json - [[Suggestion] Redact `formats` in info json with an option #455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/455#issuecomment-1367741786)
  * About subtitles in mp4 container - [Convert webvtt subtitles in mp4 into useable format #5833 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5833#issuecomment-1358246240)
  * [Find the API option for a CLI argument #5859 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5859#issuecomment-1363938900)
    * Use <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/devscripts/cli_to_api.py>
  * [[YouTube] `youtube:skip=translated_subs` doesn't work for some videos. #3875](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3875)
  * [Youtube bestvideo and vp9 preference. #1232 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1232#issuecomment-939635345)
  * [repo: git log broken by SSH signature #7322](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7322)
  * [download comments into separate comments.json file #2372 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2372#issuecomment-1506413976)
  * [How to force a conversion to a specific video codec? #7607 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7607#issuecomment-1636960750)
  * [How to download youtube videos in mp4 format? #8880](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/8880)
  * [How do I properly pass my Soundcloud oauth token to yt-dlp? #12249 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12249#issuecomment-2628937389)
  * [[youtube] 256kbps music formats not being extracted #12455 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12455#issuecomment-2677077342)
  * [[PYI-12704:ERROR] Failed to extract Cryptodome\Cipher_ARC4.pyd: decompression resulted in return code -1! #16522](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16522)
    * You probably don't have enough free disk space on the drive where your temp dir is located



**PS** : These are just the most common issues at the moment. Make sure to [search for duplicates](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) in general before opening issues. Looking at this is not an excuse to not search for other duplicates!

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

when downloading with `-o -` the frags have the temp name as `--Frag{idx}`, which if multiple processes are running in the same cwd, they will collide

[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/downloader/common.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/c7fb478d21e9e59524befbe23f7801bb267fb880/yt_dlp/downloader/common.py#L217-L222)

Lines 217 to 222 in [c7fb478](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/c7fb478d21e9e59524befbe23f7801bb267fb880)

|  def temp_name(self, filename):   
---|---  
|  """Returns a temporary filename for the given filename."""  
|  if self.params.get('nopart', False) or filename == '-' or \   
|  (os.path.exists(filename) and not os.path.isfile(filename)):   
|  return filename  
|  return filename + '.part'  
  
[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/downloader/external.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/c7fb478d21e9e59524befbe23f7801bb267fb880/yt_dlp/downloader/external.py#L174)

Line 174 in [c7fb478](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/c7fb478d21e9e59524befbe23f7801bb267fb880)

|  fragment_filename = f'{tmpfilename}-Frag{frag_index}'  
---|---  
  
I propose to add the PID as a prefix to avoid this when file is stdout, if agreed by the project, I would like to make the contribution

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

This bug report is a continuation of bug report [#15065](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15065). I opened another bug report because the current problem can be fixed in yt-dlp.

Latest version of deno now works in kde runtime flatpak but yt-dlp fails to detect its version because of different output.

yt-dlp expect deno output to be something like:-
    
    
    deno 2.9.1 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    v8 14.9.207.2-rusty
    typescript 6.0.3
    

But the outputs is something like
    
    
    Failed getting cwd: No such file or directory (os error 2)
    deno 2.9.1 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    v8 14.9.207.2-rusty
    typescript 6.0.3
    

yt-dlp expects the first line of output from deno to start with "deno" and does not recognize about output.

Patching yt-dlp to remove the first line in the above output causes yt-dlp to work as expected with deno.

Patching yt-dlp to make it read only stdout output makes yt-dlp to work as expected with deno.

The problem here seems to be yt-dlp combining deno's std out and std error streams into one stream and ending up getting confused by deno's std error output.

ffmpeg and ffprobe seems to send their version info to std error and this explains the current yt-dlp behavior and i think its wrong.

I think the solution here is for `_get_exe_version_output` method to get an argument that says what stream it should get its data.

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

"'idna' codec can't encode characters in position 0-65: label too long" というエラーが発生し、動画のダウンロードに失敗します。

原因は、abematv-licenseのnetlocが66文字あるからです。idnaのエンコードをスキップすることで、動画をダウンロードできました。

対象のURLは以下の通り：

  * ~~<https://abema.tv/video/episode/87-1000367_s1000368_p1000369>~~ (expired)
  * ~~<https://abema.tv/video/episode/87-1000639_s1000640_p1000641>~~ (expired)
  * <https://abema.tv/video/episode/87-1000810_s1000811_p1000812>
  * <https://abema.tv/video/episode/87-1000702_s1000703_p1000704>
  * <https://abema.tv/video/episode/87-1000810_s1000811_p1000974>
  * <https://abema.tv/video/episode/87-1000810_s1000811_p1001124>

# `embed-thumbnail` on MP3 downgrades ID3 verison 2.4 to 2.3 breaking date in `embed-metadata` #17186

Labels

[bugBug that is not site-specific](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22bug%22)Bug that is not site-specific[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

## Description

[](https://github.com/dot-mike)

[dot-mike](https://github.com/dot-mike)

opened [on Jul 9, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17186#issue-4850787781)

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

## Bug report

Unsure if this is specific to Windows.

When using `embed-thumbnail` with `embed-metadata` , the ID3v2.4 tags for date `TDRC` gets removed because of a ID3v2.4 downgrade to v2.3 when adding the thumbnail. This is because TDRC is not a valid v2.3 tag, so it makes sense. But the problem is that as a user I am not aware of this bug which causes me as a user to lose important metadata.

After downgrade to v2.3 we only have year `TYEAR` from `TRDC`. The date `TDAT` is missing. Probably a FFmpeg bug.

FFMpeg defaults to ID3v2.4 with the command line below for adding metadata.  
`[debug] ffmpeg command line: ffmpeg -y -loglevel repeat+info -i file:t.mp3 -map 0 -dn -ignore_unknown -c copy -write_id3v1 1 -metadata "title=Tranceparency Mixtape 001" -metadata "date=20230328" -metadata "description=The first episode of the all new Tranceparency Mixtape is here!`

But later yt-dlp proceeds to add the thumbnail using `-id3v2_version 3` option to FFMpeg breaking the existing v2.4 ID3 tag:  
`[debug] ffmpeg command line: ffmpeg -y -loglevel repeat+info -i file:t.mp3 -i file:t.jpg -c copy -map 0:0 -map 1:0 -write_id3v1 1 -id3v2_version 3 -metadata:s:v "title=Album cover" -metadata:s:v "comment=Cover (front)" -movflags +faststart file:t.temp.mp3`

## Workaround:

Force EmbedThumbnail to use v2.4 as a option: `--ppa "EmbedThumbnail+ffmpeg:-id3v2_version 4"`

Using `--ppa "ffmpeg:-id3v2_version 3"` does not work to force v2.3!

## Environment info

OS: Windows 11 x86-64.  
Build: `2026.07.04`  
ffmpeg (yt-dlp-ffmpeg build): `ffmpeg version N-124716-g054dffd133-20260531 Copyright (c) 2000-2026 the FFmpeg developers`

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    Field can not be longer than 65536 characters. See attached file!

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I'm not sure it this is the right category to post this, but as a follow-up to [#16983](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16983), there appears to be a broader issue with logins using the Spectrum MSO getting hung up about being unable to extract RelayState. [#16983](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16983) documents the problem when trying to access the History channel, or using the [aenetworks] extractor in general. I've started running into the problem with the [TBS] extractor now, too (see below). Since it looks like this is a growing issue, I decided to file a separate bug report about this issue. Thanks.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/KK-Hung)

[KK-Hung](https://github.com/KK-Hung)

opened [on Aug 24, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17527#issue-5235410020)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When using `--dump-single-json` on a BiliBili video, the returned JSON shows empty `subtitles` and `automatic_captions` fields, even though the video actually has subtitles available.

### Steps to reproduce

  1. Run: `yt-dlp --dump-single-json --cookies "cookies.txt" "https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1bB826ZEeL"`
     * Observe that `subtitles` and `automatic_captions` are both `{}`.
  2. Run: `yt-dlp --list-subs --cookies "cookies.txt" "https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1bB826ZEeL"`
     * Subtitles are listed correctly: `danmaku`, `zh`, `en`.



### Expected behavior

`--dump-single-json` should include the same subtitle metadata that `--list-subs` displays, so that tools relying on the JSON output can correctly identify available subtitles without needing a second request.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# Firefox cookie extraction doesn't take account of sqlite WAL #17601

Open

[Firefox cookie extraction doesn't take account of sqlite WAL](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17601#top)#17601

Copy link

Labels

[bugBug that is not site-specific](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22bug%22)Bug that is not site-specific[core:cookiesRelated to core cookie handling (e.g. --cookies or --cookies-from-browser)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22core%3Acookies%22)Related to core cookie handling (e.g. --cookies or --cookies-from-browser)[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

## Description

[](https://github.com/fullermd)

[fullermd](https://github.com/fullermd)

opened [on Sep 1, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17601#issue-5315542285)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When extracting cookies from Firefox, the cookies.sqlite file is copied off to a temp location and used, but the associated WAL file isn't. That means if it's been a while since a WAL checkpoint (newer firefox versions seemingly expand that window, so it's become visible) you can get stale cookies.

The following rough patch does fix it here; a real fix would need to be more careful and error-check-y etc of course. The `-shm` file doesn't, as far as I can tell from sqlite docs, have a purpose in this usage and won't need copying.
    
    
    index 08fde2cd2..4b01e140d 100644
    --- a/yt_dlp/cookies.py
    +++ b/yt_dlp/cookies.py
    @@ -1111,6 +1111,8 @@ def _config_home():
     
     def _open_database_copy(database_path, tmpdir):
         # cannot open sqlite databases if they are already in use (e.g. by the browser)
    +    database_copy_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'temporary.sqlite-wal')
    +    shutil.copy(database_path + '-wal', database_copy_path)
         database_copy_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, 'temporary.sqlite')
         shutil.copy(database_path, database_copy_path)
         conn = sqlite3.connect(database_copy_path)
    

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    WARNING: [youtube] The provided YouTube account cookies are no longer valid. They have likely been rotated in the browser as a s
    ecurity measure. For tips on how to effectively export YouTube cookies, refer to  https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extracto
    rs#exporting-youtube-cookies .

## Description

[](https://github.com/c-basalt)

[c-basalt](https://github.com/c-basalt)

  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

The dependency `websockets` defines a fatal response header accessor [`Headers.__getitem__()`](https://github.com/python-websockets/websockets/blob/e5ae728192c1b9706f0d82782482ae1ca6cd0c0a/src/websockets/datastructures.py#L128-L133) that raises `MultipleValuesError` when a header key has multiple values. Unlike `email.message.Message`, iterating on `websockets`'s `headers.items()` is fatal if any key in response header has multiple values.  
Currently `WebsocketsResponseAdapter` passes the response header as is, which is then iterated via `.items()` in `Response.__init__` and triggers `MultipleValuesError` from `websockets` dependency.  


[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/networking/_websockets.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/fdcc954df4955267ec1627cbeb347b661a110e7c/yt_dlp/networking/_websockets.py#L60)

Line 60 in [fdcc954](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/fdcc954df4955267ec1627cbeb347b661a110e7c)

|  headers=ws.response.headers,   
---|---  
  
  


[yt-dlp/yt_dlp/networking/common.py](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/fdcc954df4955267ec1627cbeb347b661a110e7c/yt_dlp/networking/common.py#L540-L541)

Lines 540 to 541 in [fdcc954](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/fdcc954df4955267ec1627cbeb347b661a110e7c)

|  for name, value in headers.items():   
---|---  
|  self.headers.add_header(name, value)   
  
  
Instead, the `Header` object from `websockets` dependency needs to be iterated by its [`raw_items()`](https://github.com/python-websockets/websockets/blob/e5ae728192c1b9706f0d82782482ae1ca6cd0c0a/src/websockets/datastructures.py#L182-L187) method

We can pre-process the headers before passing
    
    
    --- a/yt_dlp/networking/_websockets.py
    +++ b/yt_dlp/networking/_websockets.py
    @@ -54,10 +55,14 @@
     class WebsocketsResponseAdapter(WebSocketResponse):
    
         def __init__(self, ws: websockets.sync.client.ClientConnection, url):
    +        headers = Message()
    +        for name, value in ws.response.headers.raw_items():
    +            headers.add_header(name, value)
             super().__init__(
                 fp=io.BytesIO(ws.response.body or b''),
                 url=url,
    -            headers=ws.response.headers,
    +            headers=headers,

Here is a PoC to trigger the issue locally
    
    
    import threading
    import time
    
    from aiohttp import web
    from yt_dlp.networking import Request
    from yt_dlp import YoutubeDL
    
    
    def server():
        async def handler(request):
            ws = web.WebSocketResponse()
            ws.headers.add('set-cookie', 'a=1')
            ws.headers.add('set-cookie', 'b=2')
            await ws.prepare(request)
            await ws.send_str('hello')
            async for _ in ws:
                pass
            return ws
    
        app = web.Application()
        app.add_routes([web.get('/', handler)])
        web.run_app(app)
    
    
    threading.Thread(target=server, daemon=True).start()
    time.sleep(1)
    with YoutubeDL({'verbose': True}) as ydl:
        ie = ydl.get_info_extractor('Generic')
        ws = ie._request_webpage(Request('ws://127.0.0.1:8080/'), None)
        print(ws.recv())

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# netrc credentials are needlessly read multiple times per URL #16897

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[netrc credentials are needlessly read multiple times per URL](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16897#top)#16897

Copy link

Labels

[bugBug that is not site-specific](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22bug%22)Bug that is not site-specific[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

## Description

[](https://github.com/spikethehobbitmage)

[spikethehobbitmage](https://github.com/spikethehobbitmage)

opened [on Jun 7, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16897#issue-4606328086)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

This bug affects all sites that support netrc login.

`yt-dlp` reads netrc credentials twice for every network access. This can cause problems when credentials are supplied by a program or script. There are two problematic use cases:

`yt-dlp --netrc-cmd='command {}' -- "$URL1" "$URL2"`  
If `command` prompts the user for a password then the user will be prompted four times for the first URL and twice again for every following URL.

`yt-dlp --netrc --netrc-location=<( command ) -- "$URL1" "$URL2"`  
This method allows a shell function to be passed in place of an independent program. `command` is run once but only the startup check will receive login information. All downloads will proceed as if nothing was provided.

## 

The simplest solution is to save the `netrc` object between calls. It should be stored in a shared location so that multiple extractors can use the same object when URLs from more than one site are supplied on the command line.

`--netrc-cmd='command {}'` should use a dictionary of `netrc` objects keyed on the expanded `{}`. This way `command` will only be invoked once per distinct site. If `{}` is omitted it will only be called once.

`--netrc-location=` should use a single `netrc` object for all sites.

## 

This patch works as expected in all combinations of the above scenarios. As the author of this patch I hereby release it to the public domain.
    
    
    diff --git a/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py b/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py
    index 31c0266d4..9311dfc9d 100644
    --- a/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py
    +++ b/yt_dlp/extractor/common.py
    @@ -586,6 +586,7 @@ class InfoExtractor:
         _WORKING = True
         _ENABLED = True
         _NETRC_MACHINE = None
    +    _NETRC_CACHE = dict()
         IE_DESC = None
         SEARCH_KEY = None
         _VALID_URL = None
    @@ -1394,17 +1395,23 @@ def _get_netrc_login_info(self, netrc_machine=None):
             cmd = self.get_param('netrc_cmd')
             if cmd:
                 cmd = cmd.replace('{}', netrc_machine)

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I get that error when I try to download this video: <https://mediateca.educa.madrid.org/video/sgzsr1tqbgohdjyg/fs>

The HTML contains the direct link to the video, which is this: [https://mediateca.educa.madrid.org/streaming.php?id=sgzsr1tqbgohdjyg&r=org](https://mediateca.educa.madrid.org/streaming.php?id=sgzsr1tqbgohdjyg&r=org)

I guess that's why it's giving an error. But it should work since that's what the video responds with (Content-Type: video/mp4)

EDIT: Since the example url (mediateca.educa.madrid.org) is geographically restricted, I added an equivalent example to my website: <https://tomasbottari.com/yt-dlp/bug/streaming.php>

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/June-ee)

[June-ee](https://github.com/June-ee)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

us

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

TikTok has recently re-enabled a "Short dramas" entry point in the sidebar. Before this entry point was introduced, short drama videos were accessible via the regular video URL format:

Old format (works with yt-dlp): <https://www.tiktok.com/@muffindrama_us/video/7675708755559959821>

New format (not supported): <https://www.tiktok.com/shortdrama/episode/7675706520839033876/8>

When using the new /shortdrama/episode/... format, yt-dlp falls back to the generic extractor and then fails with:

text  
ERROR: Unsupported URL: <https://www.tiktok.com/shortdrama/episode/7675706520839033876/8>  
Note: This short drama entry point has appeared and disappeared before. It seems TikTok may be doing A/B testing or gradually rolling out this feature. The new URL structure appears to be a separate content system from the regular @username/video/ format.

Command used:

bash  
yt-dlp --cookies cookie.txt --impersonate chrome -o "output.mp4" <https://www.tiktok.com/shortdrama/episode/7675706520839033876/8>

I have updated yt-dlp to the latest nightly (nightly@2026.09.16 or newer) and the issue still persists.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Spain

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Description

yt-dlp fails to extract the video from an X/Twitter post with the following error:

ERROR: [twitter] 2103382268051964103: Failed to parse JSON (caused by JSONDecodeError("Expecting value in '': line 1 column 1 (char 0)"))

The error occurs while yt-dlp is attempting to retrieve the GraphQL JSON response from X.

The affected URL is:

<https://x.com/jcarlos2001/status/2103382268051964103>  
Command  
yt-dlp -f mp4 '<https://x.com/jcarlos2001/status/2103382268051964103>'  
Output  
WARNING: "-f mp4" selects the best pre-merged mp4 format which is often not what's intended.  
Pre-merged mp4 formats are not available from all sites, or may only be available in lower quality.  
To prioritize the best h264 video and aac audio in an mp4 container, use "-t mp4" instead.  
If you know what you are doing and want a pre-merged mp4 format, use "-f b[ext=mp4]" instead to suppress this warning  
[twitter] Extracting URL: <https://x.com/jcarlos2001/status/2103382268051964103>  
[twitter] 2103382268051964103: Downloading guest token  
[twitter] 2103382268051964103: Downloading GraphQL JSON  
ERROR: [twitter] 2103382268051964103: Failed to parse JSON (caused by JSONDecodeError("Expecting value in '': line 1 column 1 (char 0)")); please report this issue on <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=> , filling out the appropriate issue template. Confirm you are on the latest version using `yt-dlp -U`  
Expected behavior

yt-dlp should successfully extract the available video formats from the X/Twitter post and download the video.

Actual behavior

The Twitter extractor successfully identifies the URL and obtains a guest token, but fails when parsing the JSON returned by the GraphQL request.

Additional information

The warning concerning -f mp4 appears before the extraction error. It does not appear to be the cause of the failure; the extraction fails during the Twitter/X API response parsing stage.

The failure occurs specifically at:

Downloading GraphQL JSON

followed by:

Failed to parse JSON  
JSONDecodeError("Expecting value in '': line 1 column 1 (char 0)")

A similar Failed to parse JSON problem has previously been reported for the Twitter extractor, suggesting that changes on X's side may affect the API/GraphQL response expected by yt-dlp.

System information

Please replace the following with the output of:

yt-dlp -vU -f mp4 '<https://x.com/jcarlos2001/status/2103382268051964103>'  
WARNING: "-f mp4" selects the best pre-merged mp4 format which is often not what's intended.  
Pre-merged mp4 formats are not available from all sites, or may only be available in lower quality.  
To prioritize the best h264 video and aac audio in an mp4 container, use "-t mp4" instead.  
If you know what you are doing and want a pre-merged mp4 format, use "-f b[ext=mp4]" instead to suppress this warning  
[twitter] Extracting URL: <https://x.com/jcarlos2001/status/2103382268051964103>  
[twitter] 2103382268051964103: Downloading guest token  
[twitter] 2103382268051964103: Downloading GraphQL JSON  
ERROR: [twitter] 2103382268051964103: Failed to parse JSON (caused by JSONDecodeError("Expecting value in '': line 1 column 1 (char 0)")); please report this issue on <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=> , filling out the appropriate issue template. Confirm you are on the latest version using yt-dlp -U

Also:

yt-dlp --version  
Latest version: stable@2026.08.19 from yt-dlp/yt-dlp  
yt-dlp is up to date (stable@2026.08.19 from yt-dlp/yt-dlp)

URL

<https://x.com/jcarlos2001/status/2103382268051964103>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

_"Planet Wissen"_ is a German-language information program on all sorts of interesting general education topics.

Sometimes there is another source for the video on one of the TV channels which has broadcasted the specific program.  
For example: This [planet-wissen URL](https://www.planet-wissen.de/video-lebensglueck--was-uns-zufrieden-macht-100.html) is also available [here on this TV channel](https://www.ardmediathek.de/video/Y3JpZDovL3dkci5kZS9CZWl0cmFnLTQwNGZkMjVkLTRhM2QtNDk2MS05MWVkLTlmYTRiZTUzYWFhYQ) which is handled by the `[ARDBetaMediathek]` IE. Maybe this IE could also handle the `planet-wissen.de` URLs ?  
(I don't know, if it's always this TV channel though, or if the program runs on multiple TV channels.)

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# intelligent filename trim #6974

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[intelligent filename trim](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6974#top)#6974

Copy link

Labels

[enhancementNew feature or request](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22enhancement%22)New feature or request[triageUntriaged issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22triage%22)Untriaged issue

## Description

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

[chrizilla](https://github.com/chrizilla)

opened [on May 2, 2023](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6974#issue-1692960443)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2023.03.04** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update)) or later (specify commit)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

# problem

When a `-o` filepath\filename template consists of multiple fields, and the sum of the length of all these fields must not exceed  
`OS limit - (length of the temporary files appendix + length of yt-dlp download base path)`, the problem is how to best curtail these fields, which can vary considerably in length and are therefore unpredictable.

To simplify:  
It's difficult to ensure `A+B+C+D < OS limit` when `A`, `B`, `C`, `D` greatly vary in length.

While it is certainly possible to set a dumb limit for each field: `A.50+B.50+C.50+D.50 + base path + appendix < 255`  
this is not a intelligent solution, if for example
    
    
    A = 120 bytes
    B = 50 bytes
    C = 10 bytes
    D = 20 bytes
    

because in this case `A` will be unnecessarily truncated to less than half its length.

# example

`-o "%(alt_title,title).100B\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"`

  * `extractor` is quite short and doesn't require any further shortening
  * cutting off `id` and `format_id` makes them useless, although they can become quite lengthy in some cases
  * so that leaves us only with `alt_title` and `title` which can be shortened



The above template should work in most cases, but can still exceed the OS limit when `id` and/or `format_id` are lengthy.

# current solutions

  1. So one solution would be to add further curtailing:  
`-o "%(alt_title,title).40B\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"`  
But this shortens the video directory so severely that it becomes barely readable.

  2. `--trim-filenames` but [Behavior of --trim-filenames is not clear #3494](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494) and possibly broken:

> This should produce the file `../testfolder/Me at.webm`, but instead it produces the file `testf.webm`.
> 
> Worse still, if the `--output` argument is an absolute path like `/home/myname/folder/folder/stuff`, yt-dlp will try to create a file in the root directory called `/home/.webm`.
> 
> So, I think `--trim-filenames` is broken.

and from [“--trim-filenames” failure！pls check it. #5499 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/5499#issuecomment-1311939459) :

> the whole path will be trimmed, not only the filename. The file might end up in one of the parent directories.

so this is [not a recommended solution](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494#issuecomment-1103969834) :

> I honestly recommend using something like [outtmpl] instead to control the filename length

and [\--trim-filenames fails to clip file name properly when there is a dot in a video title #2314 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/2314#issuecomment-1011295071) :

> I am aware of this issue 😓. The `--trim-filename` option is just overall poorly implemented, making this tricky to fix. I honestly suggest using something like `%(title).30B.%(ext)s` instead

and [here](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1837#issuecomment-981907118):

> `--trim-filename` was added in youtube-dlc and actually quite buggy. I can fix this particular issue, but I recommend using the string formatting to achieve a similar effect. Eg: `-o %(title).200s.%(ext)s`




# enhancement idea

It would really be great to be able to intelligently trim the filename, i.e. trim

  1. **ONLY in case it is needed ...**  
(The idea is a bit like in [\--restrict-filenames only as fallback #6972](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6972) to use this enhancement **"only as a fallback"** in case it is needed.)

  2. **... and at a user-defined place.**  
(As opposed to `--trim-filenames` which trims at end, thereby causing the same errors in my tests as described by [@axcore](https://github.com/axcore) above in [Behavior of --trim-filenames is not clear #3494](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3494) and [@Fabian42](https://github.com/Fabian42) in [String length limit #1888](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1888):




> What currently happens if I use `--trim-filenames` is that the ID gets cut off completely if the title is too long. In the worst case, if I'm downloading a playlist of videos with titles like "Super long series title, episode 42: XYZ", I would get completely identical filenames and all downloads after the first one would get skipped.

# implemenation

The user can indicate at which position this intelligent trim should occur if needed.  
Something like:

  * `-o "%(alt_title,title).100B+\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"` : the plus sign indicates that this field can be trimmed **further** than the 100B if otherwise the entire path\filename length exceeded OS limits.
  * `-o "%(alt_title,title){100B-excesslength}\%(title).100B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"`



Maybe you'll find better implementation ideas.

It would also be a good idea to come up with some solution that would kick in by default (so that all users benefit from this enhancement and not just the 1% who dig into the jungle of parameters).

# benefits

  * If the filepath becomes too long, this enhancement would save the download from failing.
  * On the other hand, the filename length allowed by the OS can be fully used with this enhancement (as opposed to the currently possible solutions, where a "safe" filename template like `-o "%(alt_title,title).40B\%(title).40B [%(extractor)s.%(id)s] {%(format_id)s}.%(ext)s"` would waste / give away a lot of available space.
  * This would allow trimming long paths at a user-defined position where it hurts less than at the end with `--trim-filenames`.



# workaround

What I currently do is essentially going back and forth between different config files:

  * I have very generous length limits but therefore often run into filename-too-long problem.
  * I then manually increase the length limit ristriction in my config file,
  * delete the leftover files from the 1st run,
  * run yt-dlp again and ...
  * most of the time forget to reset the config file to its previous state,
  * so that the filenames of my subsequent downloads are also truncated. 🙁

### Region

Austria:yes, worldwide:maybe

### Example URLs

Example URLs are cited below, but almost all URLs expire within 7 days after broadcast so new URLs might be required.

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

## basic information

URLs from [orf:tvthek] mostly follow this pattern:

`https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/[broadcast_series]/[broadcast_series_ID]/[broadcast_episode]/[broadcast_episode_ID]`  
example:  
<https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392/Themenmontag-Die-Wahrheit-ueber-Fisch/14179024>

## problem

But [orf:tvthek] extractor doesn't yet interpret the URL as a playlist if only the playlist URL is given.  
Example:  
<https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392>  
i.e. `https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/[broadcast_series]/[broadcast_series_ID]`  
... is not recognized as a playlist.

## suggested solution

**Basically there are two different URLs listing the playlist entries:**

  * <https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392/>  
The playlist entries are listed below under the linkified header _"Weitere Ausgaben dieser Sendung"_ (german for _"more episodes of this broadcast"_), which links to the URL below ("......./episodes")
  * <https://tvthek.orf.at/profile/Themenmontag/13687392/episodes>



It would be helpful if the extractor could recognize **both** of these URLs as playlists.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

(Asking here so as not to lead [#1136](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136) further off-topic.)

In [#1136 (comment)](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1136#issuecomment-1503888641) a solution was proposed to mark truncated filenames in `-o` template:

> Add a `%(title.201&…|)s` \- read as "if `title.201` (201'th char) exists, then (`&`) add `…`, else (`|`) add nothing"

This works for character count but apparently not for the subsequently discussed byte count (which may be more useful when dealing with unicode chars):
    
    
    yt-dlp ZYlALC1Pmv4 --skip-download --no-config --print "%(title).50s%(title.51&…|)s"
    Hubble Space Telescope, Planet 9, Curiosity Mars R…    # truncates at 50 chars and detects 51st char
    
    yt-dlp ZYlALC1Pmv4 --skip-download --no-config --print "%(title).50B%(title.51B&…|)s"
    Hubble Space Telescope, Planet 9, Curiosity Mars R     # truncates at 50 bytes but doesn't detect 51st byte

I guess this is either the wrong syntax or not yet possible to do.  
In the latter case, would it be worth considering this new syntax as an enhancement ?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Exponential `--retry-sleep` is very useful, but doesn't quite work as I would have expected.

Let's look at the following example:

With

      --retry-sleep http,fragment,file_access,extractor:exp=1

    Sleeping 4096.00 seconds ...
    

I don't think this makes much sense.

If an error occurs (such as above), `--retry-sleep` sends yt-dlp to sleep, ok.  
Now, when yt-dlp wakes up from sleep and

  * ... immediately fails again, yt-dlp should be sent back to sleep and the sleep time be augmented exponentially (which is currently done)
  * ... does not immediately fail again (i.e. successfully continues to download), the **sleep time counter should be reset**.



## rationale

IMO the reason for exponential sleep time is to avoid continuously bumping into the same error with linear sleep time (i.e. trying to download every 2 seconds does not help when the server is currently down). Exponential sleep time is there sleep longer and longer and longer ... until the error goes away. But when the error has gone away, the counter should be reset, because it otherwise hampers the download unnecessarily (as shown in the example above).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[](https://github.com/chrizilla)

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)

DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Is there a guide on how to create a new extractor and/or repair a broken one ?

I searched around, but all I found was this:

  * <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors> : mum on extractor coding
  * <https://deepwiki.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/3.6-writing-custom-extractors> : AI slop ?
  * <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/2c28ee5d/CONTRIBUTING.md> : general coding guidelines



In case there is no doc yet, my question could be reclassified as feature request.

I am aware that extractors are a case-by-case thing.  
But maybe it's still possible to formulate some general strategies, promising approaches that often work, useful guidelines, etc. ?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)

Trying to download a CNN podcast episode from

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

China

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I downloaded YouTube video slices, and I found that the 2025.12.8 version could download them normally using this configuration. However, when I downloaded using the latest version of yt-dlp on a new server, I noticed that it showed success, but the file was only 1KB, which was obviously incorrect. The file also couldn't be opened. Could this be due to a cookie expiration issue?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Description

[](https://github.com/pjmattingly)

[pjmattingly](https://github.com/pjmattingly)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When attempting to install via winget (`winget install yt-dlp`), winget returns with an error:

[](https://private-user-images.githubusercontent.com/6288999/659326034-01f70583-bff4-4d89-af27-db6712149c46.png?jwt=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..KgWkf1FC0ELCIVvFsUaJ2lPdnSz-QdbRjqHN-UAZ33U)

I'm assuming this "Lech YT-DLP" is some third party provider, which may be malicious. To avoid confusion for some users, it would be helpful to revise the installation instructions to include the full ID:

`winget install yt-dlp.yt-dlp`

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

[NOTE: Im doing this on request for some one offline that wishes to remain anonymous]  
The site uses a age-gate on the main page that redirects all video page requests to it. It uses a custom video-player to overlay ads and other information.

I provided a random video, i have 0 interest in digging into the videos on the page, its mind numbing to find something that doesn't make me feel uncomfortable. However, i dont want to disrespect anyone and aid in testing.

I forked and created a example extractor (hypnotube.py)[https://github.com/EndlessEden/yt-dlp/commit/cd28499c0c8f9403a0b315bdd780fda009f1dbf9]. Feel free to use or adapt it, its messy and contains my personal notes.

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

US, Switzerland, etc

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Murrtube extractor is unable to identify the video's ID and can't start the download. Though, recently (May 8th of this year), Murrtube received a big maintenance with a server migration update, so that might have affected how videos are detected. 🤔

Edit: Here are the [page dump](https://gist.github.com/Angrones/62bbe4e6399f95de8333234c00276f16).

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I've recently been able to download age-restricted YouTube videos in 360p, even though the website offers 2160p versions. Is there a solution?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[bashonly](https://github.com/bashonly)on Aug 26, 2026

Workaround: use a [PO token provider](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide) and the `mweb` client or `web_creator` client.

This is a side effect of [#17389](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17389). The fix for that issue will also fix this one.

### Region

United Kingdom

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Every video I try to download from Eporner fails at the same step. The extractor gets as far as loading the webpage and pulling the hash out of it but then fails.

As an example this one:

[Eporner] Extracting URL: <https://www.eporner.com/hd-porn/IdFXcRMkvDU/Pregnant-Big-Tits-and-Oil-JOI/>  
[Eporner] Pregnant-Big-Tits-and-Oil-JOI: Downloading webpage  
[Eporner] Pregnant-Big-Tits-and-Oil-JOI: Downloading video JSON  
ERROR: [Eporner] IdFXcRMkvDU: Eporner said: Authorization failed. Try to reload page.

I've tried with and without cookies. Without cookies I get has failure and with cookies I get the authorisation failed.  
I've tried refreshing the cookies.  
I've tried with and without chrome browser impersonation.  
I've tried HTTP and HTTPS. If I use HTTP it just redirects to HTTPS anyway.  
I've upgraded yt-dlp to nightly 2026.09.16.232951  
and I've double checked that I can load the actual site directly via my browser which works fine.

It does sit behind age verification but my account is age verified and I can use yt-dlp fine with other sites that sit behind age verification.

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Region

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Possibly related to old issues [#14129](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14129) and [#6545](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6545). The extraction process always fail with a `403 Forbidden` error with all the URLs that I tested:

  * <https://spankbang.com/8ynaa/video>
  * <https://spankbang.com/a4yiy/video>
  * <https://spankbang.com/5fils/video>
  * <https://spankbang.com/cfgri/playlist/hoyo>



Already tried passing the `--impersonate` argument, but the result was the same. I'm not using any VPN or proxy.

Some weeks ago the scraping process worked as a charm, maybe the site recently implemented more stric restraints.

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

Spain

### Example URLs

  * Channel: <https://www.eplay.com/lewdneko/feed>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

This site is not supported, however there are many content creators that VOD there, it even allow to download them.  
As far as I can tell, the content in VOD format in this site is uploaded by the original creators and it is even possible to download manually therefore it does not break DRM nor violates copyright.

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting that yt-dlp is broken on a **supported** site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've checked that all URLs and arguments with special characters are [properly quoted or escaped](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#video-url-contains-an-ampersand--and-im-getting-some-strange-output-1-2839-or-v-is-not-recognized-as-an-internal-or-external-command)
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated

Brasil

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

On Monday, Aug 31, the script worked perfectly using this same yt-dlp build.  
I made no changes to it, and today every video I try to download hits this error.  
I've already updated the cookies file and tested on different machines, with the  
same result. The error also happens even without passing --cookies at all, which  
rules out a cookie/session issue.

This looks related to [#17403](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17403) (closed via [#17452](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/17452)), but I'm seeing the identical  
error and traceback on a build that should already include that fix, which  
suggests this may be a new regression rather than the same issue resurfacing.

# [TikTok] TikTok Web extractor ignores bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Width/Height and incorrectly maps some 540p formats to 576x1024 #16532

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[[TikTok] TikTok Web extractor ignores bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Width/Height and incorrectly maps some 540p formats to 576x1024](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16532#top)#16532

Copy link

Labels

[site-bugIssue with a specific website](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site-bug%22)Issue with a specific website[site:tiktok](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22site%3Atiktok%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/Index103000)

[Index103000](https://github.com/Index103000)

opened [on Apr 20, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16532#issue-4295235530)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

For some TikTok videos, the Web extractor derives the format resolution from `PlayAddr.UrlKey` and applies the hardcoded rule:
    
    
    if dimension == 540:  # '540p' is actually 576p
        dimension = 576

This works for some videos, but it is not always correct.

In some Web JSON responses, bitrateInfo.PlayAddr already contains explicit Width and Height fields. For these videos, the extractor currently ignores those fields and derives width / height from UrlKey + ratio instead.

As a result, some formats are reported as 576x1024 by yt-dlp, while TikTok’s own PlayAddr.Width/Height and the actual downloaded file are 540x960.

Example 1: 540p is actually 540x960

Video ID: 102363108337192960
    
    
    {
      "video": {
        "id": "102363108337192960",
        "width": 540,
        "height": 960,
        "ratio": "540p",
        "definition": "540p",
        "bitrateInfo": [
          {
            "Bitrate": 1041872,
            "GearName": "adapt_540_1",
            "PlayAddr": {
              "DataSize": "1847501",
              "Width": 540,
              "Height": 960,
              "UrlKey": "v0b044490000bo706aahv5vn4q05edv0_bytevc1_540p_1041872"
            },
            "CodecType": "h265_hvc1",
            "Format": "mp4"
          }
        ]
      }
    }

The downloaded file also reports 540x960

Example 2: 720p is actually 576x1024

Video ID: 6585786671671807238
    
    
    {
      "video": {
        "id": "6585786671671807238",
        "width": 576,
        "height": 1024,
        "ratio": "720p",
        "definition": "720p",
        "bitrateInfo": [
          {
            "Bitrate": 1258633,
            "GearName": "normal_720_0",
            "PlayAddr": {
              "DataSize": "2445150",
              "Width": 576,
              "Height": 1024,
              "UrlKey": "v090446c0000bdimjn89pog8ra75btp0_h264_720p_1258633"
            },
            "CodecType": "h264",
            "Format": "mp4"
          }
        ]
      }
    }
    

The downloaded file also reports 576x1024

Suggested fix

Prefer bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Width and bitrateInfo.PlayAddr.Height when present, and only fall back to UrlKey + ratio inference when they are missing.

This keeps the existing fallback behavior for responses that do not include PlayAddr.Width/Height, while avoiding incorrect metadata when TikTok already provides explicit per-format dimensions.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I am trying to extract videos from the following TikTok user profile:
    
    
    https://www.tiktok.com/@lelepons
    

When using the TikTok user extractor:
    
    
    yt-dlp -vU "https://www.tiktok.com/@lelepons"

yt-dlp fails with the following error:
    
    
    ERROR: [tiktok:user] lelepons: Unable to extract secondary user ID. If you are able to get the channel_id from a video posted by this user, try using "tiktokuser:channel_id" as the input URL (replacing `channel_id` with its actual value)
    

The profile is accessible on TikTok and contains public videos, so I expected yt-dlp to discover and extract the videos from the profile URL.

This appears to be related specifically to user/profile extraction and obtaining the secondary user ID.

Expected behavior:

yt-dlp should resolve the TikTok user profile and enumerate the videos posted by the account.

Actual behavior:

The `tiktok:user` extractor fails before discovering the user's videos because it cannot extract the secondary user ID.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

TikTok [very] recently added highlights to profiles, same feature as Instagram.  
So far I've only noticed it on one profile, but the strange thing is, I can only see it from one of my accounts. Looking at the same profile from a different account, I don't see the highlights. I don't follow either accounts, so I'm not sure what the requirements to view these highlights are.

Profile in question: <https://www.tiktok.com/@ydal_0>

It only seems to be visible on mobile. Screenshots attached.  
Viewing the highlights, you can't copy any links, as you can do with stories.

Whatever information is needed, I can do my best to try provide and/or find, I just don't know what to look for.
