## Description

[](https://github.com/JoseAngelB)

[JoseAngelB](https://github.com/JoseAngelB)

opened [on Sep 25, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17737#issue-5585626180)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm requesting a site-specific feature
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are playable in a browser with the same IP and same login details
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and I'm willing to share it if required



### Region

Spain

### Example URLs

<https://www.3cat.cat/3cat/trailer-de-capita-tsubasa-campions/video/6425143/>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Would it be possible to add the expiration date to the metadata?

The extractor already retrieves the metadata from the web. The same way it has the date it is put online, it has the date when it will be removed at the same place, inside "informacio".  
It has:
    
    
            data_utc = try_get(informacio, lambda x: x['data_emissio']['utc'])
            timestamp = unified_timestamp(data_utc)
    

And the expiration date should be:
    
    
            expiration_utc = try_get(informacio, lambda x: x['data_caducitat']['utc'])
            expires = unified_timestamp(expiration_utc)
    

There are videos without that field, their own ones. The ones they have limited rights have it, also they are the ones geo-restricted. I can't find any video with that field and isn't geo-restricted.

I am not sure whether this should be exposed as a 3Cat-specific field or whether yt-dlp already has, or should introduce, a standard field for media expiration dates.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    Not needed

# Windows filename sanitizer silently replaces ASCII "/" with U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS #17549

### Checklist

  * I've read the [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated
  * I'm reporting a bug unrelated to a specific site
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

On Windows 11, yt-dlp silently replaces the ASCII forward slash "/" (U+002F SOLIDUS) in metadata used by an output template with U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS.

The source title is:

Process serving Firestone (and/or)(or/and) Bridgestone on behalf of USAA per Patrick Jenks

The filename generated by yt-dlp contains:

Process serving Firestone (and[U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS]or)(or[U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS]and) Bridgestone on behalf of USAA per Patrick Jenks

Environment:

Windows 11  
yt-dlp master@2026.08.26.234438  
commit [`94eba4c`](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/94eba4c156af080e87caf10cf8ffbea03bd17407)  
win_exe  
locale cp1252  
filesystem encoding utf-8  
output encoding utf-8

The behavior reproduces both when printing the generated filename and during an actual successful HLS download.

This is not an extractor failure. The source metadata contains the normal ASCII "/" character. The substitution occurs when yt-dlp constructs a filesystem-safe filename.

The substitution is problematic because U+29F8 is visually similar to "/" but is a different Unicode character. In a downstream Windows PowerShell 5.1 workflow, the UTF-8 bytes for U+29F8 were interpreted using a legacy Windows encoding and appeared as the mojibake sequence "a-section-sign-cedilla" rather than the intended character.

I understand that "/" cannot be used literally inside a Windows filename. The issue is the silent substitution with a Unicode lookalike rather than an ASCII-safe replacement, and the lack of an obvious warning or documentation describing this transformation.

Expected behavior:

Either clearly document the filename sanitization transformation from U+002F to U+29F8, warn when the substitution occurs, or provide a clearly documented ASCII-safe filename sanitization behavior for Windows.

Actual behavior:

ASCII U+002F "/" in the source title is silently transformed into U+29F8 BIG SOLIDUS in the generated filename.

The transformation also occurs with --skip-download and --print filename, demonstrating that it occurs in filename generation rather than during HLS downloading, ffmpeg processing, or filesystem writing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

<https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed>

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

When a youtube channel input like <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> is given to yt-dlp, it parses ALL /video and /shorts, then downloads them sequentially by chronological order, latest upload first, as its what is given by the API. Its not possible to sort in any other way.

In this case, If an option like --dateafter or --datebefore is used, many unnecessary requests are sent to youtube for videos that clearly will not match a filter.

Example

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 21001231 will match 0 videos, since the earliest video is in 2024. However it will check through EVERY video, even the ones before 2024, which is unnecessary and slow.

Similarly, yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--datebefore 00010101 will also match 0 videos, but it will check every video until the very first one.

Until youtube changes this, I believe this additional checks are not necessary at all.

Therefore I suggest 2 changes.

  1. \--datebefore runs the downloading backwards, starting from the oldest video in the channel.



EDIT: an existing workaround is -I "::-1"

  2. a switch like --date-skip 5, that skips process after it has checked 5 videos and they do not match the date requirements.



Expected behaviour should then be

yt-dlp <https://www.youtube.com/@NileRed> \--dateafter 20240101 --date-skip 3

Downloads videos after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip  
Download shorts after 20240101  
skip  
skip  
skip

exit

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar issues **including closed ones**. ### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

So, here is related issue: [#6501](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/6501)

But I'm asking not about overwriting original video file, but about final (opus in case of youtube) file that being overwritten.

Example:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OcrsSaWZ4CY`  
This command download video and extract audio into 'Deja Reve.opus' file.  
Then:  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata --no-overwrites "%(title)s.%(ext)s" -w https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L8M71Xu1rVc`  
And no warnings, no errors, just overwrite of final file.

Well, it's kinda hard to tell from first glance. Same track with same name and maybe yt-dlp just overwrite metadata.  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zIAku-Qwfl0`  
`yt-dlp.exe -f bestaudio --extract-audio --audio-quality 0 --parse-metadata "%(uploader)s:%(meta_channelName)s" --embed-metadata -o "%(title)s.%(ext)s" --no-overwrites https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cBQpZsnLyMw`

Yeah, nope. End up with second track that overwrite first one. So. Is it a bug? Or intended behaviour? How to prevent such behaviour if so (except puting something like %(id)s into filename)?

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I've noticed that the stream download is often interrupted and I have to run the same command again:  
`yt-dlp --no-live-from-start https://www.youtube.com/@.../live -o "1.%(ext)s"`
    
    
    [out#0/mpegts @ 0000012fc6fb8040] video:29377kB audio:2038kB subtitle:0kB other streams:0kB global headers:0kB muxing overhead: 5.421512%
    size=   33118kB time=00:02:07.97 bitrate=2120.0kbits/s speed=0.955x
    [download] 100% of   32.34MiB in 00:02:15 at 244.46KiB/s
    [FixupM3u8] Fixing MPEG-TS in MP4 container of "1.mp4"
    

Is there anything I can do about this?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

As far as I can see, no one has posted a question like this. I know you can use the `--exec` command for symlinks. But I'm not really code savy to figure this out. This probably isn't possible but I figured it wouldn't hurt to ask.

I currently have the videos I download symlinked as `--exec 'cd "/Users/$USER/Downloads/sym-folder" && ln -s --'`. Which worked well before. All my videoes get downloaded to their own folders as `/Users/$USER/YT-Downloads/%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date>%Y-%m-%d)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s]/%(uploader)s-%(upload_date)s_%(title)s-[%(id)s].%(ext)s'` and the resulting files get symlinked to the other directory.

The thing is when I download a playlist, a folder that shows the playlist uploader gets created along with the other uploads for each video `%(uploader)s-[%(uploader_id)s]`. Which I'm fine with (I also see in the info file the playlist name and count it was with), but for the symlinked videos they just show without any filepath order. Which would make sense based on the file path. I tried using one of the fields in the OUTPUT TEMPLATE options but that didn't work properly. I figured it probably wouldn't tho.

I had asked for help for just symlinking in the past in [#11080](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11080) and based on what `bashonly` provided I tried to figure it out. He mentioned there was a field for `filepath` but I guess I had asked too many questions since he didn't answer, and I had already gotten my main question at the time answered. For symlinking he meantioned

> `ln -s -- %(filepath,_filename|)q`

but then said

> IMPORTANT: you should only ever use `%()q` in `--exec` arguments, and never `%()s`

So to sum it all up, I was wondering about a command that creates symlinks in a filepath that includes the playlist uploader. Like some sort of field string or something. I hope I didn't make this too confusing.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

##### What I want to do

When download <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6-2DAj39clo> video,  
Put the “Uploader” information in “Artist” instead of “AlbumArtist”

###### And I realized while writing this. Is this a bug?

When download <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IidyyM3giZw> with -f 251 -x option,  
in other words, if put into opus container,  
the "comment" metadata disappeared and, it put the "webpage_url" information in "description" metadata.

Please teach me what option I should write.  
I'm reading the modify metadata section but I don't quite understand it.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

Right now, most web videos on Vimeo require login to download. However, it seems that the Vimeo online player doesn't require login. The url is <https://player.vimeo.com/video/(insertvideoid)>. However, it does seem that the player url has to be open on a browser in order to be downloaded (no login required) othewis it gives 401 error. Maybe if not logged in do a redirect and tell users that the video needs to be opened in-browser if they don't wish to login so that their accounts wouldn't get banned for downloading videos? ### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

can't download few old one videos. using by any available method.  
in reason because clients (web_embedded, tv_downgraded, visionos, android, vr and other ones) get SABR and only 18 video format available or not available at all.

it can be solved using by bgutil + mweb client without cookies.  
and youtube will provide all formats. but if downloadable videos is age-restricted that a dead.end.

logs:

  1. ordinary download using by web_embedded (with cookies) SABR (format only 18).
  2. ordinary download using by yt-dlp chosing client byself. (error is The page needs to be reloaded)
  3. download using by bgutil+mweb with cookies. (download start but in a few seconds - 403 error)
  4. download using by bgutil+mweb without cookies (download can't start because age restricted video request cookies). in case with ordinary video, download will complete OK with all formats available.



BTW. i do not think the problem is GEOBLOCK or IP because if ill try ti download other one modern videos from other channel download complete OK with any requestable format.  
otherwise, ive got same download problem with other account (cookies) and even if i use VPN or TOR proxy.

It doesn't seem to be a region blocking or proxy problem that is affecting this download.

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm reporting a new site support request
  * I've verified that I'm running yt-dlp version **2022.03.08.1**. ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update))
  * I've checked that all provided URLs are alive and playable in a browser
  * I've checked that none of provided URLs [violate any copyrights](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl#can-you-add-support-for-this-anime-video-site-or-site-which-shows-current-movies-for-free) or contain any [DRM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rights_management) to the best of my knowledge
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues including closed ones. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)
  * I've read about [sharing account credentials](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#are-you-willing-to-share-account-details-if-needed) and am willing to share it if required



### Region

Spain

### Example URLs

<https://xala.cat/details/_6098449965001>

### Description

The site has movies, sports, events... The only thing I found without login needed are the trailers (accounts are free anyway), and the structure is always the same.  
I found a request the site makes to something like <https://edge.api.brightcove.com/playback/v1/accounts/5779379807001/videos/6098449965001> where the response is a json object with all the data.

### Checklist

  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)

  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

## Description

I think it's worth considering adding some info regarding using yt-dlp via GUI, instead of native, fast and less-consuming resources CLI.  
This can be done by adding some URLs for most used/suggested GUIs for yt-dlp (see below example).

## Reasons

There are 2 main scenario where a GUI would be "better" than a CLI:

  * non-technical users who may not know anything or know too little about using a terminal.
  * when you had to perform complex, difficult and long actions (=meaning long commands), so doing it in GUI it's much simple and faster.



## Example of text to show
    
    
    --list-sorted-by-most-start-public-repo--
    //This is JUST an EXAMPLE, no precise stuff.
    Suggested GUIs
    - media-downloader > GH Repo https://github.com/mhogomchungu/media-downloader 3.7K
    - ytdlp-interface > GH Repo https://github.com/ErrorFlynn/ytdlp-interface 2.4K
    - ytdlui > GH Repo https://github.com/HaredDev/YTDLUI 1
    - Hitomi-Downloader > GH Repo https://github.com/KurtBestor/Hitomi-Downloader 26.6K
    - [WEB APP] Stacher7 > Website https://stacher.io/
    - yt-dlp-gui-mac > GH Repo https://github.com/rockenlee/yt-dlp-gui-mac 30
    --list-sorted-by-most-start-public-repo--

  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

[](https://github.com/BOplaid)

### Checklist

### Region

_No response_

### Example URLs

N/A

### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

Currently there is no real documentation on the clients (e.g. `tv` and its variants, `android` and its variants, `web` and its variants, etc.) besides [the docs for the `player_client` extractor arg](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#youtube) but I would argue that that is incomplete.  
For example it doesn't specify characteristics of clients (e.g. do they need cookies? do they only provide SABR? how wide is their selection of formats compared to some other client? do they work with `--live-from-start`? etc.), why they're used (or not) instead of some other client (and an issue if applicable), etc. Also what the client actually is; for example considering there is a `web_safari` one would wonder what browser (or UA string ig) the normal `web` is. For example this sort of this description would (to my knowledge, which consists of hours of browsing through the issue tracker here) be suitable for the `android_vr` client: "Doesn't need cookies and doesn't provide SABR. Default client when cookies aren't provided (otherwise `tv_downgraded`). [Sometimes not all tracks of format 140 appear/Sometimes doesn't yield audio formats for all languages](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15756)."

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

# How to confirm Javascript runtime is correctly installed and working with yt-dlp? #15131

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Labels

## Description

[](https://github.com/superclarkk)

[superclarkk](https://github.com/superclarkk)

opened [on Nov 21, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15131#issue-3652462111)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

On a Debian 12 system, `deno` was installed under node v18.20.8 using `npm install -g deno`:
    
    
    $ which deno
    /path/to/nodejs/nvm/versions/node/v18.20.8/bin/deno
    
    $ deno --version
    deno 2.5.6 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    v8 14.0.365.5-rusty
    typescript 5.9.2
    

`yt-dlp` was installed using `pipx install "yt-dlp[default]"`:
    
    
    $ yt-dlp --version
    2025.11.12
    
    $ which yt-dlp
    /home/myuser/.local/bin/yt-dlp
    

How can I determine whether yt-dlp is using deno correctly? Also, I can find no sign of `yt-dlp-ejs` being installed, desptie installing yt-dlp with `[default]`.

As `yt-dlp` relies heavily on the javascript runtime when downloading from youtube, would it be theoretically possible for yt-dlp to have an option that shows all this information, so the user can easily confirm that their environment is configured correctly and yt-dlp is ready to rock?

For example, it could look like this:
    
    
    $ yt-dlp --version-full
    yt-dlp:     2025.11.12
    JS runtime: deno 2.5.6 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
    yt-dlp-ejs: Detected
    

Should I raise a feature request for this, assuming there's not already a solution?

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output

# [Docs] Proposal: Add warning about account risks when using cookies for YouTube in FAQ #15106

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[[Docs] Proposal: Add warning about account risks when using cookies for YouTube in FAQ](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15106#top)#15106

Copy link

Labels

[wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22wiki%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/HenryLai921)

[HenryLai921](https://github.com/HenryLai921)

opened [on Nov 19, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15106#issue-3640847947)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

I noticed that the pinned "Known Issues" ([#3766](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766)) specifically warns users that using cookies with YouTube might lead to account suspension or the "Sign in to confirm you’re not a bot" error.

However, the current FAQ section "How do I pass cookies to yt-dlp?" encourages users to pass cookies to workaround restrictions but does not currently mention this significant risk regarding YouTube accounts.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I would like to add a warning note to the FAQ section to inform users that using cookies for YouTube should be done with caution.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I plan to submit a PR to add a warning similar to the following text:

> **Note** : While cookies are useful for bypassing restrictions, **using cookies with YouTube is currently risky** and may result in your account being temporarily blocked or flagged. It is recommended to use a secondary/burner account if you must use cookies.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    N/A - This is a documentation proposal, not a bug report.

Reactions are currently unavailable

# Provide instructions for installing with pipx #16287

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Provide instructions for installing with pipx](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16287#top)#16287

Copy link

Labels

[wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22wiki%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/hb20007)

[hb20007](https://github.com/hb20007)

opened [on Mar 19, 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16287#issue-4102947455)

Issue body actions

### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar requests **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [policy against AI/LLM contributions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#automated-contributions-ai--llm-policy) and understand I may be blocked from the repository if it is violated



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

According to [PEP 668](https://peps.python.org/pep-0668/), `pipx` is the recommended way for downloading Python programs globally. The README and Wiki can be enhanced to reflect this.

Most importantly, the [“Option 1: Install the yt-dlp-ejs python package” section](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/EJS#option-1-install-the-yt-dlp-ejs-python-package) of the Wiki page on external JS scripts only mentions the command `pip install -U "yt-dlp[default]"`. I believe that `pipx` does not support upgrading a package with a specific dependency group, so instructions to download `yt-dlp` using `pipx install yt-dlp[default]` are needed.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    N/A

  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766), [the FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ), and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20-label%3Aspam%20%20) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates

  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

I have created a wiki for yt-dlp: <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki>

~~It is currently empty and I don't plan to personally add much content to this.~~ Instead, I am expecting community contributions. You can contribute by making a PR against <https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp-wiki>

* * *

Note that this is to be used as an addition to (and not a replacement for) the official documentation.

Some ideas for what it could contain:

  * Third party installation methods 
    * [Mention chocolatey for installation on Windows #4821](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/4821)
    * [Documenting third party packages #1313](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1313) / [Add AUR package to README installation instructions #1314](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/1314)
    * [README.md: Added installation via PPA instructions... #2154](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/2154)
    * [macOS Availability: MacPorts #1395](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/1395)
    * [Switch to official homebrew formula #864](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/864)
    * [Added Scoop as installation method #1112](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/1112)
  * FAQ: 
    * FAQ section from [🚨[IMPORTANT]🚨 KNOWN ISSUES/FAQ #3766](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766)
    * <https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl#faq>
    * <https://www.reddit.com/r/youtubedl/wiki>
  * GUIs, scripts, and other related tools 
    * <https://www.reddit.com/r/youtubedl/wiki/info-scripts/>
    * <https://www.reddit.com/r/youtubedl/wiki/info-guis/>
    * <https://www.reddit.com/r/youtubedl/wiki/info-forks/>
    * <https://discord.com/channels/807245652072857610/922145164108120074>
    * Plugins
  * Common commands, tips and tricks 
    * Pinned messages in <https://discord.com/channels/807245652072857610/807247901981016094>
    * Some examples from the readme can be moved to wiki?
  * How to get help 
    * Github - Bug reports and questions; You are expected to have done your due diligence
    * Discord/Matrix - Easier way to get help, but bug reports are not tracked
    * Reddit: Unofficial community

# Add a "quickstart" tutorial to the documentation/wiki #11979

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[Add a "quickstart" tutorial to the documentation/wiki](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11979#top)#11979

Copy link

Labels

[docs/meta/cleanuprelated to docs, code cleanup, templates, devscripts etc](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22docs%2Fmeta%2Fcleanup%22)related to docs, code cleanup, templates, devscripts etc[wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22wiki%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/JulesOgilvie)

[JulesOgilvie](https://github.com/JulesOgilvie)

opened [on Jan 3, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11979#issue-2766817482)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm requesting a feature unrelated to a specific site
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar issues **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Provide a description that is worded well enough to be understood

I have recently had to assist a lot of friends who are not familiar with Command Prompt in any capacity on how to use yt-dlp (ie, regular users who just want to download a playlist from youtube without the limitations of free to use websites). The readme does not seem to supply an easy to understand guide for this scenario.

An easy to understand quickstart guide would be useful for cases like this that I - and others - can point people to instead of copy-pasting instructions to. From my experience working in IT support outside of helping friends, people will be driven away from using the tool if the supplied instructions only provide complex in depth documentation and no simple quick-start guides that help users who have never had to operate similar programs/tools.

Most resources I have found online only half-explain how to use the tool and not in enough depth for completely fresh eyes to use.

This is an example of what I have told one friend before on how to use the tool:

_"To make it easier to use the yt-dlp.exe once you have downloaded the files, put the .exe in the folder you want to save the videos to, open command prompt, ensure you are on the drive you want to save to (type `cd..` to go to the "start" of your drive, then enter the letter of the drive you need if you aren't on it already)

Get to the folder you need by typing `cd`, hitting space, then use tab to navigate the folder choices and `/` to select that folder (and repeat the tab/`/` until you are where you need to be. Alternatively, you can also copy the folder directory from the top bar in the file explorer and paste that after the `cd` to get where you need to be. Hit enter and it sends you to the folder within the command prompt.

type `yt-dlp {insert the link to the video/playlist you want to download}` and it'll download everything to the folder you have inserted the /exe to"_

I do have experience with making end-user guides that are a little prettier and more understandable than the text above (it was written quickly) that have helped even the most tech-illiterate person in my office at work use command prompt so I would be willing to help with this as I believe it is something that would be of value.

### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below



### Complete Verbose Output
    
    
    No verbose output. Requesting additional documentation

# The documentation for "configuration" doesn't make any sense and needs to be rewritten #12287

New issue

Copy link

New issue

Copy link

Open

Open

[The documentation for "configuration" doesn't make any sense and needs to be rewritten](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12287#top)#12287

Copy link

Labels

[docs/meta/cleanuprelated to docs, code cleanup, templates, devscripts etc](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22docs%2Fmeta%2Fcleanup%22)related to docs, code cleanup, templates, devscripts etc[wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=state%3Aopen%20label%3A%22wiki%22)

## Description

[](https://github.com/nomino3390)

[nomino3390](https://github.com/nomino3390)

opened [on Feb 5, 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12287#issue-2833764679)

Issue body actions

### DO NOT REMOVE OR SKIP THE ISSUE TEMPLATE

  * I understand that I will be **blocked** if I _intentionally_ remove or skip any mandatory* field



### Checklist

  * I'm asking a question and **not** reporting a bug or requesting a feature
  * I've looked through the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#readme)
  * I've verified that I have **updated yt-dlp to nightly or master** ([update instructions](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#update-channels))
  * I've searched [known issues](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/3766) and the [bugtracker](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues?q=) for similar questions **including closed ones**. DO NOT post duplicates
  * I've read the [guidelines for opening an issue](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#opening-an-issue)



### Please make sure the question is worded well enough to be understood

I'm trying to make the smallest modification possible to yt-dlp - add just a -u flag when running yt-dlp with tartube. I want to do this via a config file as recommended as a valid option. However, the documentation here doesn't make sense for 90% of users.

From [the configuration section of the yt-dlp documentation](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#configuration):

  * Do I need to look for a config file that's already there, or else I'm in the wrong directory? Or do I need to create one?

  * There are five numbered categories. Will a config file in any of these categories work whenever yt-dlp is run? Or do I have to guess which location will work? Which type does tartube use?

  * There are many directories listed, even multiple per numbered category. If I can only use a config file in one of these five, and I guess the right one, can I have the config file in any of those directories, or does it depend on how yt-dlp was installed? If so, which directory do I need to use if yt-dlp is installed through tartube?



  1. Main config - I haven't given a file to --config-location

  2. Portable config - is yt-dlp installed as portable with tartube? What do they mean by "the binary?" They refuse to tell the name of the file so that people can find it. I can't find an executable file for yt-dlp anywhere in the tartube install directory. yt-dlp.conf isn't present anywhere.

  3. home config - I didn't "give a path to p" and this refuses to tell me what "home directory" they're talking about ie an actual folder name and what files will be in it (there are six folders with "yt-dlp" in the tartube install directory and for 90% of users, none of them have signs as being the home directory for yt-dlp)

  4. user config - ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME} means nothing and no part of it can be used in windows>run like %appdata% can be. ${APPDATA} means nothing. Do they mean %appdata% or appdata? Which one? They take you to different directories when entered in windows>run and neither have any yt-dlp files in them. ~ doesn't tell me what directory to use

  5. system config - [There are six "etc" folders in the tartube installation](https://imgur.com/RdPCvZh), how would I know which one to use? None of them have a yt-dlp folder in them, so why is this listed as two options?




### Provide verbose output that clearly demonstrates the problem

  * Run **your** yt-dlp command with **-vU** flag added (`yt-dlp -vU <your command line>`)
  * If using API, add `'verbose': True` to `YoutubeDL` params instead
  * Copy the WHOLE output (starting with `[debug] Command-line config`) and insert it below

## Question

I'm running the following command:
    
    
    yt-dlp -x -f 'ba*' --format-sort 'abr,codec' 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nzLw6GMQ65I'
    

As a result, I get a 2.9MB `.m4a` file. When I pass `-F` it shows an ABR of `0k` (format ID 22).

If I instead use `-f 'ba'`, I get 3.3MB `.opus` file. Shouldn't `ba*` have selected this `.opus` file to begin with, since it's larger?

Reactions are currently unavailable

# Supported sites

Below is a list of all extractors that are currently included with yt-dlp. If a site is not listed here, it might still be supported by yt-dlp's embed extraction or generic extractor. Not all sites listed here are guaranteed to work; websites are constantly changing and sometimes this breaks yt-dlp's support for them. The only reliable way to check if a site is supported is to try it.

The zipimport Unix executable contains code licensed under ISC and MIT. The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/fdec00e0bf530dc6c3cc7b1dd780e95d9ae460e9/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum _recommended_ Python version has been raised to 3.11**  
\- Since Python 3.10 will reach its end-of-life in October 2026, support for it will be dropped soon. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16916)
  * **The official Windows release binaries will soon require Windows 10 or later.** [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16917)
  * Security: [[CVE-2026-55404](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-55404)] [Downstream command injection via improper sanitization of --write-link output](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-6v4j-43gg-vj32)  
\- Shortcut file data is now properly validated and sanitized when the `--write-link` options are used

#### A description of the various files is in the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#release-files)

The zipimport Unix executable contains code licensed under ISC and MIT. The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/7f7bdc974dc61d941d1a0d51c4e21a0fdb7b2d06/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

* * *

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum supported versions of Deno, Node, and Bun have been raised.**  
The minimum required version of [Deno](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16767) is now `v2.3.0`; supported [Node](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16765) versions are `v22` and up; [Bun support has been deprecated](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16766) and limited to versions `1.2.11` through `1.3.14`.
  * Security 
    * Usage of vulnerable conversions (e.g. `%()s`) with the `--exec` option is an all-too-common pitfall. To remedy this, `--exec` now only allows safe conversions in its command templates. 
      * Most users can simply replace `%(...)s` with `%(...)q` in their `--exec` argument(s). Numeric conversions are unaffected by this change. Using unsafe conversions with `--exec` poses a significant security risk. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-69qj-pvh9-c5wg)
    * [[CVE-2026-50019](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50019)] [File Downloader cookie leak with curl](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-f7j3-774f-rfhj)
      * Impact is limited to users of `--downloader curl`; cookies are now properly passed to curl so that it respects their scope
    * [[CVE-2026-50023](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50023)] [Dangerous file type creation via insufficient filename sanitization](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-c6mh-fpjc-4pr3)
      * Writing files with the extensions `.desktop`, `.url`, or `.webloc` is now only allowed in the context of `--write-link` functionality
    * [[CVE-2026-50574](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50574)] [Arbitrary code execution via manifest downloads with aria2c](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-vx4q-3cr2-7cg2)
      * Impact is limited to users of `--downloader aria2c`
      * Support for downloading HLS and DASH formats with aria2c has been removed. Users affected by this change should migrate to use `-N` for concurrent fragment downloads via the native downloader

The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/fdec00e0bf530dc6c3cc7b1dd780e95d9ae460e9/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum _recommended_ Python version has been raised to 3.11**  
\- Since Python 3.10 will reach its end-of-life in October 2026, support for it will be dropped soon. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16916)
  * **The official Windows release binaries will soon require Windows 10 or later.** [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16917)
  * Security: [[CVE-2026-55404](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-55404)] [Downstream command injection via improper sanitization of --write-link output](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-6v4j-43gg-vj32)  
\- Shortcut file data is now properly validated and sanitized when the `--write-link` options are used

#### A description of the various files is in the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#release-files)

The zipimport Unix executable contains code licensed under ISC and MIT. The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/7f7bdc974dc61d941d1a0d51c4e21a0fdb7b2d06/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum supported versions of Deno, Node, and Bun have been raised.**  
The minimum required version of [Deno](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16767) is now `v2.3.0`; supported [Node](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16765) versions are `v22` and up; [Bun support has been deprecated](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16766) and limited to versions `1.2.11` through `1.3.14`.
  * Security 
    * Usage of vulnerable conversions (e.g. `%()s`) with the `--exec` option is an all-too-common pitfall. To remedy this, `--exec` now only allows safe conversions in its command templates. 
      * Most users can simply replace `%(...)s` with `%(...)q` in their `--exec` argument(s). Numeric conversions are unaffected by this change. Using unsafe conversions with `--exec` poses a significant security risk. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-69qj-pvh9-c5wg)
    * [[CVE-2026-50019](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50019)] [File Downloader cookie leak with curl](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-f7j3-774f-rfhj)
      * Impact is limited to users of `--downloader curl`; cookies are now properly passed to curl so that it respects their scope
    * [[CVE-2026-50023](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50023)] [Dangerous file type creation via insufficient filename sanitization](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-c6mh-fpjc-4pr3)
      * Writing files with the extensions `.desktop`, `.url`, or `.webloc` is now only allowed in the context of `--write-link` functionality
    * [[CVE-2026-50574](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50574)] [Arbitrary code execution via manifest downloads with aria2c](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-vx4q-3cr2-7cg2)
      * Impact is limited to users of `--downloader aria2c`
      * Support for downloading HLS and DASH formats with aria2c has been removed. Users affected by this change should migrate to use `-N` for concurrent fragment downloads via the native downloader

#### Important changes

  * **Login with OAuth is no longer supported for YouTube**  
Due to a change made by the site, yt-dlp is no longer able to support OAuth login for YouTube. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11462#issuecomment-2471703090)

#### Important changes

  * **Beginning with this release, yt-dlp's Python dependencies _must_ be installed using the `default` group**  
If you're installing yt-dlp with pip/pipx or requiring yt-dlp in your own Python project, you'll need to specify `yt-dlp[default]` if you want to also install yt-dlp's optional dependencies (which were previously included by default). [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/11255)
  * **The minimum _required_ Python version has been raised to 3.9**  
Python 3.8 reached its end-of-life on 2024.10.07, and yt-dlp has now removed support for it. As an unfortunate side effect, the official `yt-dlp.exe` and `yt-dlp_x86.exe` binaries are no longer supported on Windows 7. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10086)

#### Important changes

  * **Following this release, yt-dlp's Python dependencies _must_ be installed using the `default` group**  
If you're installing yt-dlp with pip/pipx or requiring yt-dlp in your own Python project, you'll need to specify `yt-dlp[default]` if you want to also install yt-dlp's optional dependencies (which were previously included by default). [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/11255)
  * **py2exe is no longer supported**  
This release's `yt-dlp_min.exe` will be the last, and it's actually a PyInstaller-bundled executable so that yt-dlp users updating their py2exe build with `-U` will be automatically migrated. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10087)

#### Important changes

  * Security: [[CVE-2026-26331](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-26331)] [Arbitrary command injection with the `--netrc-cmd` option](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-g3gw-q23r-pgqm)
    * The argument passed to the command in `--netrc-cmd` is now limited to a safe subset of characters

[github-actions](/apps/github-actions) released this  07 Jan 14:31 

[ 2021.01.07  ](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/tree/2021.01.07)

[ `5d0c537`](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/5d0c5371414b8e39b1288cbc80197921c45660b5)

Changelog: Initial Release

#### 2021.01.05

  * **Format Sort:** Added `--format-sort` (`-S`), `--format-sort-force` (`--S-force`) - See [Sorting Formats](https://github.com/pukkandan/yt-dlp#sorting-formats) for details
  * **Format Selection:** See [Format Selection](https://github.com/pukkandan/yt-dlp#format-selection) for details 
    * New format selectors: `best*`, `worst*`, `bestvideo*`, `bestaudio*`, `worstvideo*`, `worstaudio*`
    * Changed video format sorting to show video only files and video+audio files together.
    * Added `--video-multistreams`, `--no-video-multistreams`, `--audio-multistreams`, `--no-audio-multistreams`
    * Added `b`,`w`,`v`,`a` as alias for `best`, `worst`, `video` and `audio` respectively
  * **Shortcut Options:** Added `--write-link`, `--write-url-link`, `--write-webloc-link`, `--write-desktop-link` by [@h-h-h-h](https://github.com/h-h-h-h) \- See [Internet Shortcut Options](https://github.com/pukkandan/yt-dlp#internet-shortcut-options) for details
  * **Sponskrub integration:** Added `--sponskrub`, `--sponskrub-cut`, `--sponskrub-force`, `--sponskrub-location`, `--sponskrub-args` \- See [SponSkrub Options](https://github.com/pukkandan/yt-dlp#sponskrub-options-sponsorblock) for details
  * Added `--force-download-archive` (`--force-write-archive`) by by h-h-h-h
  * Added `--list-formats-as-table`, `--list-formats-old`
  * **Negative Options:** Makes it possible to negate boolean options by adding a `no-` to the switch 
    * Added `--no-ignore-dynamic-mpd`, `--no-allow-dynamic-mpd`, `--allow-dynamic-mpd`, `--youtube-include-hls-manifest`, `--no-youtube-include-hls-manifest`, `--no-youtube-skip-hls-manifest`, `--no-download`, `--no-download-archive`, `--resize-buffer`, `--part`, `--mtime`, `--no-keep-fragments`, `--no-cookies`, `--no-write-annotations`, `--no-write-info-json`, `--no-write-description`, `--no-write-thumbnail`, `--youtube-include-dash-manifest`, `--post-overwrites`, `--no-keep-video`, `--no-embed-subs`, `--no-embed-thumbnail`, `--no-add-metadata`, `--no-include-ads`, `--no-write-sub`, `--no-write-auto-sub`, `--no-playlist-reverse`, `--no-restrict-filenames`, `--youtube-include-dash-manifest`, `--no-format-sort-force`, `--flat-videos`, `--no-list-formats-as-table`, `--no-sponskrub`, `--no-sponskrub-cut`, `--no-sponskrub-force`
    * Renamed: `--write-subs`, `--no-write-subs`, `--no-write-auto-subs`, `--write-auto-subs`. Note that these can still be used without the ending "s"
  * Relaxed validation for format filters so that any arbitrary field can be used
  * Fix for embedding thumbnail in mp3 by [@pauldubois98](https://github.com/pauldubois98)
  * Make Twitch Video ID output from Playlist and VOD extractor same. This is only a temporary fix
  * **Merge youtube-dl:** Upto [2020.01.03](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/commit/8e953dcbb10a1a42f4e12e4e132657cb0100a1f8) \- See [blackjack4494/yt-dlc#280](https://github.com/blackjack4494/yt-dlc/pull/280) for details
  * Cleaned up the fork for public use



#### 2021.01.05-2

  * **Changed defaults:**
    * Enabled `--ignore`
    * Disabled `--video-multistreams` and `--audio-multistreams`
    * Changed default format selection to `bv*+ba/b` when `--audio-multistreams` is disabled
    * Changed default format sort order to `res,fps,codec,size,br,asr,proto,ext,has_audio,source,format_id`
    * Changed `webm` to be more preferable than `flv` in format sorting
    * Changed default output template to `%(title)s [%(id)s].%(ext)s`
    * Enabled `--list-formats-as-table`



#### 2021.01.07

  * Removed priority of `av01` codec in `-S` since most devices don't support it yet
  * Added `duration_string` to be used in `--output`
  * Created First Release

The zipimport Unix executable contains code licensed under ISC and MIT. The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/7f7bdc974dc61d941d1a0d51c4e21a0fdb7b2d06/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum supported versions of Deno, Node, and Bun have been raised.**  
The minimum required version of [Deno](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16767) is now `v2.3.0`; supported [Node](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16765) versions are `v22` and up; [Bun support has been deprecated](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16766) and limited to versions `1.2.11` through `1.3.14`.
  * Security 
    * Usage of vulnerable conversions (e.g. `%()s`) with the `--exec` option is an all-too-common pitfall. To remedy this, `--exec` now only allows safe conversions in its command templates. 
      * Most users can simply replace `%(...)s` with `%(...)q` in their `--exec` argument(s). Numeric conversions are unaffected by this change. Using unsafe conversions with `--exec` poses a significant security risk. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-69qj-pvh9-c5wg)
    * [[CVE-2026-50019](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50019)] [File Downloader cookie leak with curl](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-f7j3-774f-rfhj)
      * Impact is limited to users of `--downloader curl`; cookies are now properly passed to curl so that it respects their scope
    * [[CVE-2026-50023](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50023)] [Dangerous file type creation via insufficient filename sanitization](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-c6mh-fpjc-4pr3)
      * Writing files with the extensions `.desktop`, `.url`, or `.webloc` is now only allowed in the context of `--write-link` functionality
    * [[CVE-2026-50574](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50574)] [Arbitrary code execution via manifest downloads with aria2c](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-vx4q-3cr2-7cg2)
      * Impact is limited to users of `--downloader aria2c`
      * Support for downloading HLS and DASH formats with aria2c has been removed. Users affected by this change should migrate to use `-N` for concurrent fragment downloads via the native downloader

[github-actions](/apps/github-actions) released this  24 Feb 21:13 

[ 2021.02.24  ](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/tree/2021.02.24)

[ `c74d1aa`](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/c74d1aa3404e837b2c7e14c509125237630efc11)

### Important

The module name have been changed from `youtube_dlc` to `yt_dlp` and the binary name from `youtube-dlc` to `yt-dlp`. Take care to modify your programs/scripts to work with this change in name

### Changelog:

  * Moved project to an organization [yt-dlp](https://github.com/yt-dlp)
  * **Completely changed project name to yt-dlp** by [Pccode66](https://github.com/Pccode66) and [pukkandan](https://github.com/pukkandan)
    * Also, `youtube-dlc` config files are no longer loaded
  * **Merge youtube-dl:** Upto [commit/4460329](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/commit/44603290e5002153f3ebad6230cc73aef42cc2cd) (except tmz, gedi)
  * [Readthedocs](https://yt-dlp.readthedocs.io) support by [shirt](https://github.com/shirt-dev)
  * [youtube] Show if video was a live stream in info (`was_live`)
  * [Zee5] Add new extractor by [Ashish](https://github.com/Ashish0804) and [pukkandan](https://github.com/pukkandan)
  * [jwplatform] Add support for `hyland.com`
  * [tennistv] Fix extractor
  * [hls] Support media initialization by [shirt](https://github.com/shirt-dev)
  * [hls] Added options `--hls-split-discontinuity` to better support media discontinuity by [shirt](https://github.com/shirt-dev)
  * [ffmpeg] Allow passing custom arguments before -i using `--ppa "ffmpeg_i1:ARGS"` synatax
  * Fix `--windows-filenames` removing `/` from UNIX paths
  * [hls] Show warning if pycryptodome is not found
  * [documentation] Improvements 
    * Fix documentation of `Extractor Options`
    * Document `all` in format selection
    * Document `playable_in_embed` in output templates

[github-actions](/apps/github-actions) released this  19 Feb 21:47 

[ 2021.02.19  ](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/tree/2021.02.19)

[ `4524baf`](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/4524baf056c1611cea44ab5ebeb6cd8da82da6da)

Changelog:

  * **Merge youtube-dl:** Upto [commit/cf2dbec](https://github.com/ytdl-org/youtube-dl/commit/cf2dbec6301177a1fddf72862de05fa912d9869d) (except kakao)
  * [viki] Fix extractor
  * [niconico] Extract `channel` and `channel_id` by [kurumigi](https://github.com/kurumigi)
  * [youtube] Multiple page support for hashtag URLs
  * [youtube] Add more invidious instances
  * [youtube] Fix comment extraction when comment text is empty
  * Option `--windows-filenames` to force use of windows compatible filenames
  * [ExtractAudio] Bugfix
  * Don't raise `parser.error` when exiting for update
  * [MoveFiles] Fix for when merger can't run
  * Changed `--trim-file-name` to `--trim-filenames` to be similar to related options
  * Format Sort improvements: 
    * Prefer `vp9.2` more than other `vp9` codecs
    * Remove forced priority of `quality`
    * Remove unnecessary `field_preference` and misuse of `preference` from extractors
  * Build improvements: 
    * Fix hash output by [shirt](https://github.com/shirt-dev)
    * Lock python package versions for x86 and use `wheels` by [shirt](https://github.com/shirt-dev)
    * Exclude `vcruntime140.dll` from UPX by [jbruchon](https://github.com/jbruchon)
    * Set version number based on UTC time, not local time
    * Publish on PyPi only if token is set

* * *

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum _recommended_ Python version has been raised to 3.10**  
Since Python 3.9 will reach end-of-life in October 2025, support for it will be dropped soon. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13858)
  * **darwin_legacy_exe builds are being discontinued**  
This release's `yt-dlp_macos_legacy` binary will likely be the last one. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13856)
  * **linux_armv7l_exe builds are being discontinued**  
This release's `yt-dlp_linux_armv7l` binary could be the last one. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13976)

* * *

#### Important changes

  * **Default behaviour changed from`--mtime` to `--no-mtime`**  
yt-dlp no longer applies the server modified time to downloaded files by default. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12780)
  * Security: [[CVE-2025-54072](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-54072)] [Fix `--exec` placeholder expansion on Windows](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-45hg-7f49-5h56)
    * When `--exec` is used on Windows, the filepath expanded from `{}` (or the default placeholder) is now properly escaped

#### Important changes

  * **New option`--preset-alias`/`-t` has been added**  
This provides convenient predefined aliases for common use cases. Available presets include `mp4`, `mp3`, `mkv`, `aac`, and `sleep`. See [the README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/README.md#preset-aliases) for more details.

[ `fdec00e`](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/fdec00e0bf530dc6c3cc7b1dd780e95d9ae460e9)

[](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#installation "Installation instructions") [](https://discord.gg/H5MNcFW63r "Discord") [](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/Maintainers.md#maintainers "Donate") [](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/tree/2026.07.04#readme "Documentation") [](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp-nightly-builds/releases/latest "Nightly builds") [](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp-master-builds/releases/latest "Master builds")

#### A description of the various files is in the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#release-files)

The zipimport Unix executable contains code licensed under ISC and MIT. The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/fdec00e0bf530dc6c3cc7b1dd780e95d9ae460e9/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

* * *

#### Important changes

  * **The minimum _recommended_ Python version has been raised to 3.11**  
\- Since Python 3.10 will reach its end-of-life in October 2026, support for it will be dropped soon. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16916)
  * **The official Windows release binaries will soon require Windows 10 or later.** [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16917)
  * Security: [[CVE-2026-55404](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-55404)] [Downstream command injection via improper sanitization of --write-link output](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/security/advisories/GHSA-6v4j-43gg-vj32)  
\- Shortcut file data is now properly validated and sanitized when the `--write-link` options are used



### Changelog

#### Core changes

  * [Always include warnings in debug output](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/d23e6f5a387d5933bc24e1eb5437da8fd563c1f0) ([#17059](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17059)) by [bashonly](https://github.com/bashonly)
  * [Fix `allow-unsafe-ext` compat option](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/e47691215f75fe7e9684080d17fadf340c9a8450) ([#16920](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16920)) by [bashonly](https://github.com/bashonly)
  * [Raise minimum recommended Python version to 3.11](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/7b03011294c0210802ffc901390006c39152b999) ([#17034](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/17034)) by [bashonly](https://github.com/bashonly)

#### A description of the various files is in the [README](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp#release-files)

The zipimport Unix executable contains code licensed under ISC and MIT. The PyInstaller-bundled executables are subject to these and other licenses, all of which are compiled in [THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/5977782142ca7e41240f07202cc9b8dcc087b401/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt)

* * *

#### Important changes

  * **An external JavaScript runtime is now required for full YouTube support**  
yt-dlp now requires users to have an external JavaScript runtime (e.g. Deno) installed in order to solve the JavaScript challenges presented by YouTube. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15012)

* * *

#### Important changes

  * **A stopgap release with a _TEMPORARY partial_ fix for YouTube support**  
Some formats may still be unavailable, especially if cookies are passed to yt-dlp. The _**NEXT**_ release, expected very soon, **will require an external JS runtime (e.g. Deno)** in order for YouTube downloads to work properly. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/14404)
  * **The minimum _required_ Python version has been raised to 3.10**  
Python 3.9 has reached its end-of-life as of October 2025, and yt-dlp has now removed support for it. [Read more](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13858)

#### Workflow file for this run

[ .github/workflows/release-nightly.yml ](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/66f49765d5a46c7be1c2c414f245c71530c4a2fd/.github/workflows/release-nightly.yml) at [66f4976](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/66f49765d5a46c7be1c2c414f245c71530c4a2fd)

[ ](/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/edit/master/.github/workflows/release-nightly.yml)

This file contains hidden or bidirectional Unicode text that may be interpreted or compiled differently than what appears below. To review, open the file in an editor that reveals hidden Unicode characters. [Learn more about bidirectional Unicode characters](https://github.co/hiddenchars)

| name: Release (nightly)  
---|---  
| on:  
|  schedule:  
|  \- cron: '23 23 * * *'  
|  workflow_dispatch:  
|   
| permissions: {}  
|   
| jobs:  
|  check_nightly:  
|  name: Check for new commits  
|  if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || vars.BUILD_NIGHTLY  
|  permissions:  
|  contents: read  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-latest  
|  outputs:  
|  commit: ${{ steps.check_for_new_commits.outputs.commit }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1  
|  with:  
|  fetch-depth: 0  
|  persist-credentials: false  
|   
|  \- name: Retrieve HEAD commit hash  
|  id: head  
|  shell: bash  
|  run: echo "head=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" | tee -a "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"  
|   
|  \- name: Cache nightly commit hash  
|  uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0  
|  env:  
|  SEGMENT_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MINS: 1  
|  with:  
|  path: .nightly_commit_hash  
|  key: release-nightly-${{ steps.head.outputs.head }}  
|  restore-keys: |  
|  release-nightly-  
|   
|  \- name: Check for new commits  
|  id: check_for_new_commits  
|  shell: bash  
|  run: |  
|  relevant_files=(  
|  "yt_dlp/*.py"  
|  ':!yt_dlp/version.py'  
|  "bundle/*.py"  
|  "bundle/docker/compose.yml"  
|  "bundle/docker/linux/*"  
|  "bundle/requirements/*"  
|  "pyproject.toml"  
|  "Makefile"  
|  ".github/workflows/build.yml"  
|  ".github/workflows/release.yml"  
|  ".github/workflows/release-nightly.yml"  
|  )  
|  if [[ -f .nightly_commit_hash ]]; then  
|  limit_args=(  
|  "$(cat .nightly_commit_hash)..HEAD"  
|  )  
|  else  
|  limit_args=(  
|  \--since="24 hours ago"  
|  )  
|  fi  
|  echo "commit=$(git log --format=%H -1 "${limit_args[@]}" -- "${relevant_files[@]}")" | tee -a "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"  
|   
|  \- name: Record new nightly commit hash  
|  env:  
|  HEAD: ${{ steps.head.outputs.head }}  
|  shell: bash  
|  run: echo "${HEAD}" | tee .nightly_commit_hash  
|   
|  release:  
|  name: Publish GitHub release  
|  needs: [check_nightly]  
|  if: needs.check_nightly.outputs.commit  
|  permissions:  
|  contents: write # May be needed to publish release  
|  id-token: write # Needed for trusted publishing  
|  uses: ./.github/workflows/release.yml  
|  with:  
|  prerelease: true  
|  source: ${{ (github.repository != 'yt-dlp/yt-dlp' && vars.NIGHTLY_ARCHIVE_REPO) || 'nightly' }}  
|  target: 'nightly'  
|  secrets:  
|  ARCHIVE_REPO_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ARCHIVE_REPO_TOKEN }}  
|  GPG_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.GPG_SIGNING_KEY }}  
|   
|  publish_pypi:  
|  name: Publish to PyPI  
|  needs: [release]  
|  if: vars.NIGHTLY_PYPI_PROJECT  
|  permissions:  
|  id-token: write # Needed for trusted publishing  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-latest  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Download artifacts  
|  uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1  
|  with:  
|  path: dist  
|  name: build-pypi  
|   
|  \- name: Publish to PyPI  
|  uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@dc37677b2e1c63e2034f94d8a5b11f265b73ba33 # v1.14.2  
|  with:  
|  verbose: true

| name: Label Handler

|  types: [labeled] # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]  
|   
| permissions: {}  
|   
| concurrency:  
|  group: label  
|  cancel-in-progress: false  
|  queue: max  
|   
| env:  
|  GH_TELEMETRY: "false"  
|  LLM_MESSAGE: >-  
|  This contribution has been determined to be in violation of yt-dlp's  
|  [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy).  
|  Repeat or flagrant violations of this policy will result in a permanent ban from this repository.  
|  BAD_MESSAGE: >-  
|  This contribution has been determined to be in violation of yt-dlp's  
|  [policy against supporting sites that are primarily used for  
|  piracy](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy).  
|  Please consult the [yt-dlp wiki  
|  FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#why-is-there-a-rule-against-websites-primarily-used-for-piracy)  
|  if you have questions.  
|   
| jobs:  
|  issue-llm:  
|  name: Issue (ai-policy-violation)  
|  if: github.event.issue.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'ai-policy-violation')  
|  permissions:  
|  issues: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock issues  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock issue  
|  run: |  
|  gh issue unlock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh issue close "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --reason "not planned" --comment "${LLM_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh issue lock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|   
|  issue-bad:  
|  name: Issue (piracy/illegal)  
|  if: github.event.issue.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'piracy/illegal')  
|  permissions:  
|  issues: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock issues  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock issue  
|  run: |  
|  gh issue unlock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh issue close "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --reason "not planned" --comment "${BAD_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh issue lock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|   
|  pr-llm:  
|  name: PR (ai-policy-violation)  
|  if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ai-policy-violation')  
|  permissions:  
|  pull-requests: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock PRs  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock PR  
|  run: |  
|  gh pr unlock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh pr close "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --comment "${LLM_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh pr lock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|   
|  pr-bad:  
|  name: PR (piracy/illegal)  
|  if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'piracy/illegal')  
|  permissions:  
|  pull-requests: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock PRs  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock PR  
|  run: |  
|  gh pr unlock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh pr close "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --comment "${BAD_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh pr lock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

| name: Label Handler  
---|---  
| on:  
|  issues:  
|  types: [labeled]  
|  pull_request_target:  
|  types: [labeled] # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]  
|   
| permissions: {}  
|   
| concurrency:  
|  group: label  
|  cancel-in-progress: false  
|  queue: max  
|   
| env:  
|  GH_TELEMETRY: "false"  
|  LLM_MESSAGE: >-  
|  This contribution has been determined to be in violation of yt-dlp's  
|  [**NO AI / NO LLM POLICY**](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#no-ai--no-llm-policy).  
|  Repeat or flagrant violations of this policy will result in a permanent ban from this repository.  
|  BAD_MESSAGE: >-  
|  This contribution has been determined to be in violation of yt-dlp's  
|  [policy against supporting sites that are primarily used for  
|  piracy](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#is-the-website-primarily-used-for-piracy).  
|  Please consult the [yt-dlp wiki  
|  FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ#why-is-there-a-rule-against-websites-primarily-used-for-piracy)  
|  if you have questions.  
|   
| jobs:  
|  issue-llm:  
|  name: Issue (ai-policy-violation)  
|  if: github.event.issue.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'ai-policy-violation')  
|  permissions:  
|  issues: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock issues  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock issue  
|  run: |  
|  gh issue unlock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh issue close "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --reason "not planned" --comment "${LLM_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh issue lock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|   
|  issue-bad:  
|  name: Issue (piracy/illegal)  
|  if: github.event.issue.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'piracy/illegal')  
|  permissions:  
|  issues: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock issues  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock issue  
|  run: |  
|  gh issue unlock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh issue close "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --reason "not planned" --comment "${BAD_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh issue lock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|   
|  pr-llm:  
|  name: PR (ai-policy-violation)  
|  if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ai-policy-violation')  
|  permissions:  
|  pull-requests: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock PRs  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock PR  
|  run: |  
|  gh pr unlock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh pr close "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --comment "${LLM_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh pr lock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|   
|  pr-bad:  
|  name: PR (piracy/illegal)  
|  if: github.event.pull_request.state == 'open' && contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'piracy/illegal')  
|  permissions:  
|  pull-requests: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock PRs  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}  
|  PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}  
|  steps:  
|  \- name: Comment, close and lock PR  
|  run: |  
|  gh pr unlock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" || true  
|  gh pr close "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --comment "${BAD_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh pr lock "${PR_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"

|  Please consult the [yt-dlp wiki

|  permissions:  
|  issues: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock issues  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

|  gh issue close "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --reason "not planned" --comment "${LLM_MESSAGE}"  
|  gh issue lock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|

|  issues: write # Needed to comment on, close, and lock issues  
|  runs-on: ubuntu-slim  
|  env:  
|  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

|  gh issue lock "${ISSUE_NUMBER}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}"  
|

|  \- name: "Lock new issue"

| name: Release (nightly)

| on:  
|  schedule:  
|  \- cron: '23 23 * * *'  
|  workflow_dispatch:
